candidate_relations.reason: The record identifies migrated gastric-band erosion with obstruction and perforation, not primary small-bowel ischemia.
The imaging and prior bariatric device point to migrated band complications rather than appendicitis.
Small-bowel obstruction is present, but adhesion or stricture conflicts with migration of an eroded gastric band as the cause.
Mechanical jejunal obstruction and perforation are not gastroparesis.
Jejunal perforation is part of the composite diagnosis but omits band erosion, migration, and obstruction.
The obstruction was caused by a migrated gastric band rather than adhesions.
Band slippage is related to the device but differs from erosion with intraluminal migration, obstruction, and perforation.
Bowel ischemia is not the documented mechanism of the migrated-band obstruction and perforation.
Free gas arose from jejunal perforation associated with band migration, not a peptic ulcer.
The dense tubular migrated device and obstruction do not support mesenteric ischemia.
This captures band erosion, jejunal migration, and perforation but omits the required intestinal obstruction.
Gastric-band complication is compatible but omits erosion, migration, jejunal obstruction, and perforation.
The lesion and migrated device are jejunal rather than diverticular.
The tubular shadow represents migrated gastric-band material, not an adhesional band.
No imaging or operative features support intussusception.
Intestinal obstruction is present but omits the eroded migrated band and jejunal perforation.
The perforation was jejunal and related to band migration, not a duodenal ulcer.
There is no ectopic gallstone; the obstructing structure is migrated gastric-band material.
The record documents perforation from migrated-band obstruction rather than intestinal ischemia as the final object.
This exactly matches the erosion, jejunal migration, obstruction, and perforation described in the reference.
